title: Start small they said, so I did!
author: ZtehnoSkapra
selftext:
I clearly suck at video editing, but I just released a little something into the wild and wanted to share it.

This game actually started as an Easter egg I put into our internal company mobile app built with Expo + Skia. It unexpectedly blew up, with colleagues fighting for podium spots on the leaderboard. So when the Fable preview was released publicly, I decided to give it a try and turn that little Easter egg into a proper mobile game.

Fable ported it to Godot in about 20 minutes. From there, I slowly started replacing the assets (GPT Image 2 ended up being the most consistent), adding new features, and building out more game modes.

The whole thing took far more time than I’m willing to admit. I still wonder how people seem to “one-shot” all those impressive demos I keep seeing on socials.  
But in the end, I think it was worth it as my little daughter enjoys the game so much that she’s already beaten my high score, haha.

We’ve already started working on another project together, since she seems to enjoy the whole process of turning ideas into playable prototypes and testing stuff out.

So I guess I’ll see you around again soon :)

replies.body: Thx, I love cartoon-like games so I tried to create one. I’m pretty happy with the result :)

comments.author: Lordxb
comments.body: How did I get art like that from image it’s not video!!!

replies.author: ZtehnoSkapra
replies.body: Start with concept art, then pick single image you like the most and use that as reference for additional assets. GPT Image is pretty good at generating images based on another image, but it usually takes a few tries. For the animated faces, generating a whole sheet of different expressions was key to keep them consistent.

comments.body: Making anything good actually takes time, even if AI can speed you up. Congrats I’d love to try it out, it looks fun! Did you code the original Easter egg  yourself?

replies.author: ZtehnoSkapra
replies.body:
Yeah since frontend and mobile apps is what I do for over a decade, but when it comes to physics and shaders, that’s where AI helped a ton. I could probably never create such cool electric vfx myself and Fable nailed it within minutes, it’s crazy.

Seems like I forgot to include the game name, lol, it’s called Sparky Grind. It’s out on App Store, but I’m still waiting for the final approval on Google Play as they require official beta test which slows the process down by two weeks for Android. Hopefully soon :)
